ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Answer the following two questions based on this pedigree for the biochemical disorder known as alkaptonuria. Affected individuals are unable to break down a substance called alkapton, which colors the urine black and stains body tissues. Otherwise, the condition is of no consequence. Males are shown as squares, females as circles. Afflicted individuals are shown in black. If there is a carrier condition, it is not displayed.
Which of the following statement is supported by the information given in the pedigree?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text: If parents 1 and 2 in row II have another child, the chance that the child would be afflicted with alkaptonuria is 25%.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: If parents 1 and 2 in row II have another child, the chance that the child would be afflicted with alkaptonuria is 25%.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the pedigree chart, on the right side of row II there is a pair of parents: individual 1 is an unfilled circle, indicating an unaffected female; individual 2 is an unfilled square, indicating an unaffected male. After the two mate, in row III there is one offspring, shown as a filled circle, indicating having alkaptonuria. Reasoning: The question asks the probability that if this same pair of parents in row II has another child, that child will be affected. Alkaptonuria is conventionally autosomal recessive inheritance. Two unaffected parents producing an affected child shows that both parents must be heterozygous carriers, namely Aa and Aa. The offspring genotype ratio of Aa × Aa is AA 25%, Aa 50%, aa 25%. The affected genotype is aa, so the probability that each new child is affected is 25%.
